The main takeaway from our work is that

, in many applications where a two-groups model with covariates is of interest, a nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimator, which is easily implementable via the expectation-maximization algorithm, achieves a near-optimal rate of convergence.
in a wide range of problems in statistics, the nonparametric maximum-likelihood approach is a robust and scalable tool that can be easily implemented via the EM algorithm.

the nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimator can be used to estimate the unknown parameter in a two-component mixture model in the presence covariates with near parametric rate of convergence, without the need to specify the dimension of the covariates, and without the need to tune any parameters.
